newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-BOURSE SEES 20 MORE FIRMS LISTED IN YEAR.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-BOURSE SEES 20 MORE FIRMS LISTED IN YEAR.

text.p: The stock exchange expects that the number of companies quoted on the bourse could grow by 20 over the next 12 months and market capitalisation may double, Helo Meigas, bourse managing director, said on Wednesday.
"I believe 20 companies is not too much of an overestimate," Meigas told Reuters in an interview.
"At the same time we think market capitalisation will not grow by 20 percent as the companies are small...and do not add much to liquidity," she added.
"Market capitalisation may double in a year," she said.
There are 10 companies listed on the Tallinn stock exchange and eight on the free market. Current market capitalisation is 13.6 billion kroons.
Most of the companies heading for the stock exchange are in the service and industry sector, Meigas said.
"It is very difficult to make forecasts on infrastructure companies but I think that some things might happen this year," Meigas said.

She also said that the bourse wanted to list foreign firms on the free market. She said the stock exchange was particularly interested in Latvian and Lithuanian companies as more information was available.
"It would be too risky to bring Russian companies," she added. She said it was not yet clear whether foreign companies could be listed.
